  • K per skill — "weapon power" in the skill table = character phys/magic power from sections 1-2 · but skill % versus normal attacks is still unset.
  • Alignment multiplier vs Element power — see elements.md (next ruling needed: this gate leaves Element damage at ~35% of physical damage)

Glossary glossary.md

238 lines · imports 0 · generated none

Glossary

The shared language of the design. Every spec file uses these words with exactly these meanings — when two systems disagree, it is usually because one of them used a word loosely.

How to read a row: what the term is · what it decides · what it is not, or what it is most often confused with. Values are not typed here; the number lives in tools/data/ and the doc that prints it owns the figure.

The 3 Layers of an Item

One item answers 3 separate questions. They are separate on purpose: collapsing any two of them makes an item unreadable.

LayerAnswersDecided byNot decided by
Rarityhow many Mods the item hasdrop roll (Common / Rare)anything about the values inside them
Item qualitywhich value range every Mod on it rolls inthe drop source, with level as a ceilingRarity
Tierwhich sub-range inside that rangeItem quality alone — one item has one Tier set, shared by all its Modsthe individual Mod
Common · mid quality
  ├── T3  Physical power flat  37-43
  ├── T2  Str flat             15-16
  └── T1  Evasion %            10-11
  • Rarity never touches a rolled value. A high-quality Common must beat a low-quality Rare, or Rarity would be the more important axis.
  • Item quality is one value for the whole item. Every Mod rolls from the same range set — a Mod cannot borrow another Mod's quality.
  • Tier is a property of the item, not of a Mod. Two Mods on one item are always inside the same sub-range set.

Attack and Defend Layers

A layer is one step of the calculation, in a fixed order. Two words that are constantly confused:

  • Offensive / Defensive are Mod pools — which Mods may roll on which slot (equipment-slot.md).
  • Attack layer / Defend layer are the runtime order — what happens to one number, in sequence (combat.md §2).

A layer either removes the hit, reduces the damage, scales it, or receives it. Knowing which kind a layer is tells you what it can and cannot answer.

Attack layers (we hit a mob)

#LayerKindWhat it decidesWhat it cannot do
1hit_chanceremovesaccuracy ÷ (accuracy + mob evasion) — whether the hit exists at allnever reaches 100% by design
2critscalesphysical hits only, ×(1 + crit_damage/100 − 1) · excess chance becomes crit damagemagic and the 5 Elements never crit
3Weakscales×1.5 when our Element matches the mob's Innate elementnot the same thing as the Element counter table
4Element counterscalesthe Element-versus-Element multiplierdoes not apply to physical
5bleedadds over timephysical DoT from a physical hit, no Element tagdoes not stack, armour ignores it, cannot crit
6mob HPreceiveswhat is left after layers 1-5—

The three damage paths — physical, magic, Element — are added together before layers 2-4 scale them, so a Weak Element hit and a crit are two different multiplications on one number.

Defend layers (a mob hits us)

#LayerKindWhat it decidesWhat it cannot do
1perfect dodgeremovesnot contested — deletes the hit outrightcannot be opposed, so accuracy does not touch it
2evasionremovesmob accuracy vs our evasion rating, and Cappedcannot block a DoT tick or an unconditional effect
3splitdivides50% physical + 50% the mob's Innate Elementthe two halves then meet different layers
4armourreducesthe physical half only, by PoE's rationever touches the Element half, never touches DoT
5Elemental resistancereducesthe Element half only, per Elementnever touches the physical half, never stops a debuff
6damage takenscalesthe one multiplier that runs after every reductioncannot make a hit miss
7Energy Shieldreceivestakes the mitigated number before HPchaos bypasses it
8statusaddsthe mob's Element status, gated by its Alignmentres does not block this
9HPreceivesthe remainderHP is a receiver, never a reducer

Three consequences worth remembering, because most defensive confusion comes from them:

  • The order is the rule. Layers 1-2 decide whether the hit exists, so nothing later can be wasted on a miss; layers 4-6 shrink what survived them; layers 7 and 9 are the only pools.
  • Armour and resistance never overlap. They meet different halves of the split, which is why a build cannot max one and ignore the other.
  • Every Element debuff bypasses resistance. Layers 4-5 shrink damage; layer 8 hands you burn, chill, shock, poison or mark regardless. Holy veil exists to answer exactly that.

Item and Mod Vocabulary

TermMeaning
RarityHow many Mods an item carries: Common or Rare. A crafted item may reach the Rare maximum. Not a quality measure.
Item qualitylow / mid / high — the value range every Mod on the item rolls in, comparable to Path of Exile item level. Not how good the item feels; it is a range.
TierThe sub-range inside a quality. T1 is the best. Not an item level, not per-Mod.
ModOne rolled stat line on an item, read as name value (Tier) — e.g. Physical power flat 45 (T2).
FlatA value added straight into the stat before any % modifier runs. Str flat 24 adds 24 to Str.
%A multiplier applied to the finished stat. Str % 5 makes the whole Str total 5% larger. Flat lands first, then % multiplies it.
Stat ModThe Mods that are neither Offensive nor Defensive — Stat Mod flat, rolling any of the 7 Core stats. It rolls on every item and no slot blocks it; the Stat Mod % sibling is retired (D-114).
OffensiveAttack-side Mods. Roll on weapon slots only.
DefensiveDefence-side Mods. Roll on the 10 non-weapon slots only.
Legacy modSlots 1-2 of a dropped item, fixed at drop. The Remove mod stone can never target them, and an added Mod (slots 6-7) is never legacy.
Gear ModA piece's own inherent defence value — Armour, Evasion or Energy Shield, decided by its Base school. Raised only by a Quality Stone. Never a Mod: Reroll, Refine, Remove and Add cannot touch it, and it is always shown on its own top line, never inside the Mod list.
BaseThe frame of one slot (mail / plate / vestments). Decides weight and which Mods are Primary or Secondary. Decides nothing else — not Mod count (that is Rarity), not rolled values (that is quality + Tier).
Quality floor / ceilingThe lowest and highest Item quality one drop source is allowed to emit. A ceiling still rolls the whole range below it; best is never guaranteed.
WeightCarried by the item from its Base, multiplied by quality. Not a rolled value.
CapacityHow much weight a build can carry, set by Str. Going over does not lock slots — it cuts Attack speed, up to a limit (formula.md section 11).

Stats and Formulas

TermMeaning
Core statThe 7 attributes: str / vit / dex / agi / wis / int / lck. Every item can raise all of them through Stat Mods.
K valueA hidden constant that converts a stat into a game value — K_STR is physical power per point of Str. Set by design, invisible to the player, and never retyped into prose.
CapThe ceiling on a stat. Every Cap must be proven reachable from the real Mod tables — an unreachable Cap is not a limit, it is a number that lies to the player (formula.md reachability table). Not every stat has one: Critical chance and Accuracy deliberately have none.
AlignmentDex, spent twice: it is the gate that lets a status land, and the multiplier on that status's damage. One value, both jobs.
Physical power / Magic powerDamage derived from the character (formula.md sections 1-2). There is no "weapon Base power" — every weapon draws its damage from the character alone.
Elemental powerThe third damage path, derived from Int and gated by nothing but the weapon's own Element (elements.md).
hit_chanceaccuracy ÷ (accuracy + evasion) — the chance a hit connects at all. Never 100% by design: the ratio caps itself.
crit overflowCritical chance has no Cap. Chance stops at 100% and everything above it becomes crit damage, so stacking more crit is never wasted.
damage takenA multiplier that runs after every mitigation layer and before any pool. Armour and resistance each shrink something; evasion and Perfect dodge remove the hit before this ever sees it; this scales what survived them (combat.md section 2).
global damage / global defend / global speedThe three reserved umbrella multipliers (engine.json global). global damage scales outgoing damage once, after weak / Element counter / crit; global defend is the incoming step-6 damage_taken bucket; global speed scales the whole clock (the Haste aura) and is player-only — no mob carries Haste. All start at ×1.00 — a future source feeds one bucket, so they never stack as separate multipliers.

Combat

TermMeaning
PushHP reaching zero is not death. The fighter is pushed out of combat, rests for Max HP ÷ (hp_regen × 8) seconds, then walks back in alone. Losing time is the only thing this game charges.
No deathStanding rule. Defensive value comes from time not lost, not from survival. Reinstating death would mean rewriting the whole defensive half.
CampThe Push rest location, and nothing else — the settlement that owns the current zone. Never a general word for a base.
DoTDamage over time, ticking once a second. All Element DoT shares one budget (elements.md section 6).
LeechHP returned as a percentage of damage just dealt.
Perfect dodgeRemoves the hit outright and is not contested — the only answer to things Evasion cannot block, such as DoT ticks and unconditional effects. Chance comes from Lck as a ratio, with a Cap just under the top that ratio reaches (the generated Cap table in formula.md prints both).
ReachHow far a build can act. There is no map, no tiles and no movement: near and far are a queue (combat.md section 2b).
EliteA rarity flag, not a size — an Elite is a Large body carrying its own stronger numbers, so two multipliers never stack.
Attack layer / Defend layerOne step of the damage calculation in its fixed order (combat.md §2). Not the same thing as an Offensive or Defensive Mod, which is a Mod pool. A layer removes the hit, reduces the damage, scales it, or receives it.

Elements and Statuses

TermMeaning
Elementfire / cold / lightning / poison / chaos. One item holds exactly one Element, and that Element decides which status the item can inflict.
Innate elementA mob's home Element. It takes ×1.5 damage from that Element and attacks us with that Element, so one preparation answers both halves.
WeakThe ×1.5 bonus when our Element matches a mob's Innate element. A relationship between two things — not the same thing as the Element counter table.
Counter elementThe multiplier one Element deals to another (0.60 resisted, 1.20 strongest). Table in elements.md.
burn (fire)Damage over time that also cuts the target's HP regen, 10% of it per stack, to a limit set by the stack Cap.
chill (cold)Cuts the target's attack speed and accuracy, and cuts its Armour.
shock (lightning)Stops the target's clock, cuts its attack speed, and cuts our own Alignment against that target — the one status that fights our own.
poison (poison)Stacking damage over time that decays slowly and survives a weapon swap.
mark (chaos)A growing multiplier on the hit it rides, plus leech. The only status with no damage term of its own.
bleedPhysical damage over time, copied from Path of Exile. Not an Element: no Element tag, no resistance, no counter row. Does not stack, a new application refreshes it, armour does not reduce it, and it cannot crit.

Crafting

TermMeaning
RerollRe-rolls the value inside a Mod, staying in the same Tier. A tool for fixing a bad line, not for climbing power.
RefineRaises a Mod one Tier.
AscendRaises Item quality one step for the whole item.
Remove mod stoneDeletes one random non-legacy Mod.
Add mod stoneFills one empty slot by drawing from the item's own Base pool. Always random — the stone draws, the player does not choose.
Quality StoneThe only source of Gear Mod points.
Tier stoneFeeds Reroll tier and Refine.
Reroll value stoneThe cheapest stone, minted by dissolving junk.
Corrupt stone / Repair stoneBoss-only and elite/boss-only, one use per piece. The rarest stones in the game.
UpgradeAdds Gear Mod points to a piece, one step at a time, with rising failure odds. Low steps are safe; the top steps can Break a piece — unequippable, stats zero, kept at its level. Protection absorbs a break before it happens. Online only.
CorruptOne gamble per piece, in the Vaal style: a roll that can take the piece somewhere better or ruin it. A corrupted piece accepts no further stones, so it is a one-way door.
SalvageBulk disposal of gear below the filter line, with a bounded milestone payout. It creates no new income type.
Bag filterWhat makes every drop a decision: Keep it (it beats the equipped piece in the same slot on at least one axis), Dissolve it for a Reroll value stone, or Sell it for gold. One piece pays one medium, never both.
adventure bagThe 50-slot bag of kept gear carried while adventuring (1 piece per slot, weight counted). Full = pickups pause; nothing auto-converts. Deposit is town-only (loot.md section 4).
character bagThe 30-slot bag of carried consumables: stones stack 999/slot and are weightless, herbs and potions stack 100/slot and weigh 0.1/unit, gold takes no slot.
stashTown storage, organisation only, bought with gold (towns.md). Never grants power and never auto-converts.
herbA plant drop, consumed rather than equipped or sold. Always kept by the filter — it never dissolves. Its rate feeds the herbalist's demand and the pouch ladder.
junkA flavoured drop from each species (Rat Tail, Golem Shard…), always kept, stacks 999/slot and is weightless, and is sold to the Settlement Counterhand for gold — gold's primary mint (Ragnarok-style). Has three rarities (common · uncommon · rare): rarer junk is dearer and drops less often, so expected gold per kill is flat. Not gear, not a stone.

Town and Economy

TermMeaning
SettlementA named place holding services and NPCs. Never holds combat. Also the name of the state the player is in while there — the counterpart to Adventure (below).
Adventure / SettlementThe two states. Adventure = in a zone: combat, loot, the adventure bag fills; no crafting and no deposit. Settlement = in a settlement: deposit, stash, craft, restock; no combat. Neither is the same as AFK/active — a character can be AFK in either state.
CapitalA settlement serving one quality band with the full service set. Three in total.
ZoneThe combat area attached to a settlement, always the world.md zone 1-9. A settlement never replaces a zone.
RoadThe link between two settlements. Travel only, and its content exists only in opt-in mode.
WaypointA Road made instant after visiting its settlement once.
StandingA per-settlement unlock counter earned from the flows that already exist. Never spendable, never a currency, never grants a stat.
GoldThe quality-of-life medium, minted by exactly two things: selling a filter-rejected piece, and a bounded Road event. Buys space, time, information and appearance — never power.
Collector setA named bundle of gear pieces a settlement wants handed in, one per Base school. The reward is a convenience — a banner, a stash tab, a title — never power, and some sets are paid for in gold.
ReservationAn aura holding back a share of Max Mana. Nothing drains per second; the player opens the set, and total reservation may not reach the whole pool.
reserve tierThe share of the pool one aura holds back (skill-pool-aura-heal.md). Only auras reserve — no other skill does.

Mobs

TermMeaning
speciesA creature lineage (Rat · Husk · Drake). Decides a stat multiplier vector, an accuracy tier and a damage type. Not a class, and not zone-locked: the same species at a higher level is the same species.
body classThe four mob sizes — Small · Medium · Large · Boss (engine.json mob.sizes). Decides HP, damage-taking and evasion multipliers and whether it can appear in a group: only Small and Medium form groups, Large and Boss appear alone. Elite is not a body class — it is a rarity flag forced onto a Large body.
Base schoolThe three armour families a Base can belong to - light (Evasion), heavy (Armour), cloth (Energy Shield). It decides the Gear Mod a piece carries, and it is what a Collector set is built from.
weapon groupThe three families a weapon belongs to - melee, ranged, magic. It decides which attack skills can use the weapon and which stat the weapon scales. A dagger is melee, not ranged.
EliteA rarity flag on a Large body, not a fifth size. Spawns as its own event and drops its own stone.
mob accuracyDerived from the mob's own stats through the same K values the player uses, scaled by the species accuracy tier. This is why Evasion works against some species and is nearly worthless against others.

Abbreviations

A closed set. An abbreviation is the same term shortened, never a second name for it — so a term with no row here has no abbreviation, and inventing one is a synonym, which AGENT.md section 2 forbids. A new row is added only when the abbreviation is actually used in a doc or a tool, and a rejected spelling is recorded in aliases.json (guarded by lint L4). Every row must survive lint L8: one abbreviation per term, one term per abbreviation, and each abbreviation used somewhere in the repo.

TermAbbreviationCanonical in
Attack speedaspdengine.json caps.aspd · docs
Cooldown reductioncdrengine.json caps.cdr · docs
Critical chancecritformula-offense.md · engine.js
Physical powerphysengine.json K_STR · docs
Elemental powerelemengine.json K_ELEM · docs
Damage per secondDPSformula.md section 0 · docs
Elemental resistancerescore-stats.md · docs
Elemental alignmentaligncore-stats.md · docs
Accuracyaccformula-utility.md section 8 · engine.js
Evasionevworld.md mob sheet · engine.js
Energy ShieldESformula-defense.md section 5 · engine.js
Max HPHPformula-defense.md section 5 · docs
Max Manampengine.json K_INT_MP · engine.js
Damage over timeDoTelements.md section 6 · docs
ExperienceXPworld.md XP table · engine.json xp

Terms That Must Not Be Interchanged

Do not writeWrite instead
item TierItem quality
qualityRarity
status resistanceelemental resistance
status alignmentelemental alignment
Attack speed (times/sec)Attack speed (%) — aspd is a percentage and its Cap lives in engine.json
flat resnothing — res is % only
flat crit chancenothing — crit chance is % only, has no Cap, and its excess becomes crit damage
Core stat ModStat Mod — the Mods that are neither Offensive nor Defensive. "Core stat" on its own still names the 7 attributes.
SP / SP pool / SP regenmana / Max Mana / mana regen — this game says mana, never SP
the two pre-Mod names for an item stat lineMod — aliases.json holds the deprecated spellings

Rules That Must Not Be Broken

  1. Never say Tier means Item quality — Tier is the sub-range, quality is the large range.
  2. Never tie value ranges to Rarity — a high-quality Common must be able to beat a low-quality Rare.
  3. Never let Mods on one item pull from different range sets — one item, one quality, one Tier set.
  4. Never swap quality and Rarity.
  5. Tier is not required on every Mod — when a range is too narrow to split readably, drop the Tier and keep the three quality levels.
  6. One source pays one medium — a piece yields a Reroll value stone or gold, never both, and no gold↔stone exchange exists anywhere.
  7. Gold never buys power — space, time, information and appearance only. Gear, Mods, potions and stones are not for sale at any NPC.
  8. Never type a derived number into a second document — it lives in tools/data/, a writer prints it, and tools/anchors.ts fails when a copy multiplies.

Value Reading Examples

ModReads as
Physical power flat 45 (T2)Mid quality, middle sub-range — decent, not rare.
Physical power flat 78 (T1)High quality, best sub-range — an item to push immediately.
Str flat 8 (T3)Low quality, lowest sub-range — a temporary unlock piece.

Harness harness/HARNESS.md

132 lines · imports 0 · generated none

Harness

Agent operating rules for this repo. Adapted from the Continental-Idle harness; the shape is borrowed, the values are ours.

Why this file exists: coding agents fail in predictable ways — they lose the thread mid-task, run the wrong checks, and declare victory early. The rules below are the counter.

Division of ownership: this file owns agent behaviour. AGENT.md owns this project's rules, terminology bans, and the doc layout. Neither restates the other.

Read chain

  1. AGENT.md — project rules. Read first.
  2. This file — how to work.
  3. glossary.md — shared language. Read when a term is load-bearing; patch it when one locks.
  4. harness/todo.md — the single work file: what is open, and what is in flight right now. Read at

task start.

  1. harness/decisions.md — what was ruled and why. Only when the user asks about a past decision.

Never read harness/decisions.md to decide the current task; it is history, not instruction.

Design docs live under doc/<layer>/ (see AGENT.md §4); they are addressed by bare name (glossary.md), so the files above are found at doc/start/glossary.md etc.

Verify routing

node tools/verify.ts is the only verify entry point and it is pre-authorised. Run it after any edit, fix what your change broke, rerun without asking. Do not run it to "check whether it is worth running" — it always is.

It runs twelve cages in order: engine (check), town, skills, tree, ladder, loot, bases, timeline, survival, inventory, anchor, and doc lint. The last one is the referential-integrity pass over the markdown — it is what catches a file you moved or a name you retyped.

Rebuild the views after a doc edit: node tools/report.ts (dashboard) and node tools/wiki.ts build. The writer that owns a generated block is the --write flag of that block's cage.

One command for the whole build: node tools/build.ts runs every writer, then verify, then both views and stops at the first failure (--check skips the writers and only verifies + rebuilds). Use it unless you are fixing one specific cage.

Mid-task re-anchor: after roughly eight file edits, or after any context cutoff, re-read harness/todo.md. If the open work no longer matches what you are doing, fix the file before editing again.

The work file

harness/todo.md is the single work file — there is no second slot and no per-topic scratch file. It holds two things and nothing else:

  • Open work — what is not built yet, split by who can close it.
  • One line naming what is post-release and deliberately not tracked.

The shape of the repo, where the numbers live, and the standing rules are AGENT.md's job (§0 project phase · §4 structure), not the work file's — the work file names work and nothing else.

Write it silently after a meaningful step: a user order, a context shift, a root cause, a landed choice. Do not narrate the write.

Clearing the slate

When work is done, the line is deleted — not ticked, not struck through, not summarised as "recently closed". A work file that accumulates finished items stops being a work file: it becomes a changelog nobody reads, and the next session has to wade through it to find the three things still open.

  • The record of what was done lives in harness/decisions.md, with the gate that holds it. That

is the one place a finished thing is allowed to still exist.

  • Never write a closing paragraph in place of deleting the line. A tidy summary of completed work

is the same clutter in nicer clothes.

  • A parked task (moved to post-release, or waiting on an owner ruling) is a single line under the

post-release note — never left to rot in the open list.

  • If a line turns out to be already true when you re-read it, delete it on the spot.

Tooling

Use the tool that answers the question instead of editing a doc to find out.

  • See a value's effect without editing docs — node tools/skills.ts --calc --stat N --power N --level N --cdr N --ladder N prints dmg/press · eff cd · presses/sec · mana%/s for every attack skill, and node tools/report.ts carries the same as a live "Skill workshop" section. Both read tools/lib/skillmodel.ts.
  • Edit data through the wiki editor when a form is faster than the JSON — node tools/wiki.ts serve --open (loopback only) renders every tools/data/*.json collection as a validated form, then runs the writers + every cage + lint and rolls back on failure. Direct JSON edits work too.
  • Rename a skill or aura — change the name in skills.json, add "Old Name": "New Name" to its renames map, then run node tools/tree.ts --write; the node Enables cells update themselves. tools/tree.ts --checks reports any cell still on an old name as PENDING until you do. Never retype the name into a doc.

History

harness/decisions.md is the log. One entry per finished thing, newest first, shaped:

| D-0NN | applied | what was decided, and the numbers that moved | the files that carry it |

Rules:

  • Log when done, never in advance. Not questions asked, not audits that changed nothing, not parked ideas.
  • A direction decision is part of its entry, not a separate file. There is no second decision log.
  • Routine fixes and refactors are not logged. If a change is not worth remembering, do not record it.
  • A rule that closes a queue line must be logged with the gate that enforces it — a ruling with no

guard is a comment, not a decision.

Report format

Verdict line first: <task> — DONE | PARTIAL | BLOCKED (<n>/<total>). Then Changed / Decisions / Gaps ((none) when empty) / Verify with the exact command and its result. Every item carries a status tag so "did it change?" is never inferred. No tables. Audits are read-only and say so.

Decisions and asking

  • Decide, don't stall. A reversible in-repo choice is made now and logged as veto-able —

including unrequested scope growth, new tooling, and interface picks. A veto is a normal follow-up.

  • Ask only for: a change to the game's rules that the owner must rule on, anything irreversible,

and genuinely missing information. Asking is the last resort.

  • Look it up, never ask for a fact. Every number in this repo is computed by a cage; if a fact is

not in the data, say so rather than estimating.

  • Claim then impact: when the user reports a problem, verify it against the docs first and state

what is actually true before changing anything.

Scope

Fix what was asked. Unrequested cleanup is a separate ask, even when it is obviously right — this repo has spent a session collapsing duplicate data on purpose, and doing that uninvited is the same mistake in the other direction.

If the requested change turns out to be much larger than it looked, say so before starting rather than three files in.

Zero duplication

Never create a second home for a fact that already has one. If a number lives in tools/data/, the writer prints it; a second document restating it is a defect, not a convenience. The same goes for a glossary, a decision log, and a work file — one each, and this repo has already deleted the duplicates that used to exist.

Decisions

Append-only log of design rulings that were actually applied. A patch that changes the specs is recorded here with a status so its rationale survives after the patch file is deleted. Newest first.

idstatusdecisionlands in
D-121applied · veto-ableA new buff, Energy Absorb, converts a share of every incoming hit into Energy Shield — and that share is negated from HP either way. The owner named the skill (absorb 15%-30% of damage into Energy Shield instantly · duration 3 sec · cd 20 sec) and ruled two points: the ramp is linear from 15% at skill level 1 to 30% at level 20, and the absorbed share is always removed from HP whether or not the shield has room — a press on a full shield must still be a real defence, so the ES refill is a capped bonus and never the point of the press. The row carries es_absorb_pct 15 and es_absorb_cap 30 (two new members of EFFECT_STATS); mobSwing gains a trailing optional absorbPct and returns absorbed, taken off the hit before the ES split; esAbsorbPct(sk) ramps base→Cap off the buff's own skill level, Ghost Dance's pattern; game.ts banks absorbed into the shield capped at pool. The buff-set meta line loses its hard-coded timing (buffs no longer share one cd/duration), the roster prose says seven, and the skill-count note loses its stale pre-redesign totals. This is new power not yet folded into mob_HP — the debt is booked on checks.md D34 (H1), same as the other six buffs and the Haste aura. The folder is a shelf, not part of the address: every import <file>.md, prose citation <file>.md and cage read stays bare, so none of the ~700 code references or the prose citations had to change. The one lever is new in tools/lib/generated.js — docIndex() scans the root, doc/ recursively and harness/, resolveDoc(key) maps a bare name to its path (and passes non-doc paths such as tools/data/*.json through), and listDocs/read/write run on top of it. Direct reads were repointed at the resolver in state.js · lint.js · report.js · anchors.js · bases.js · check.js · inventory.js · lib/engine.js · lib/store.js and wiki.js (/raw/ + recursive watch); the wiki nav gained Techstack.md and mob-roster.md, previously unsorted. D-118applied · veto-ableA displayed percentage is capped at 2 decimals — final_pct is the only value that exceeded it. The owner asked to limit decimals to two places. final_pct (e.g. 142.836) is the sole value over 2 decimals in both the client's skills panel and the generated skill-pool-attack.md table, and both printed it raw. The cap is display-only: tools/skills.js (pct2) and game/src/App.svelte (pct2) round with Math.round(x * 100) / 100, which caps without forcing trailing zeros (145.19 stays 145.19). tools/data/skills.json keeps full precision because engine/skills.js reads final_pct for cast damage — rounding the data would shift in-game press damage by ~0.004% and risk exact-match gates, so the number's home is untouched and only its two projections change. The attack table was regenerated; its press/damage columns are unmoved. D-117applied · veto-ablenpm run check is green, and the App.svelte failure was an upstream svelte2tsx heuristic, not the plugin version. C1 suspected @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte 5.1.1 being two majors behind, but the registry holds no newer svelte-check (4.7.6) or svelte (5.57.1), so no bump exists. The real cause is sveltejs/svelte#13715 (open, unfixed): the bundled svelte2tsx decides whether $state/$derived/$props is a rune or a store subscription partly by whether a declared variable name contains the rune's name; a top-level let state in App.svelte therefore made every $state read as the phantom store $state, injected let $state = __sveltets_2_store_get(state), and typed the whole panel any ('state' implicitly has type 'any', Block-scoped variable '$state' used before its declaration). Bisected with throwaway probe components; <svelte:options runes={true} /> and compilerOptions.runes do not prevent it. The documented workaround — rename the colliding binding — is applied: state → gameState throughout App.svelte (the WHY is kept as a one-line comment at the declaration), and the same pass fixed the genuine stale-UI findings the gate surfaced (Dodge / perfect dodge rows re-pointed at caps.evasion / caps.perfect_dodge, TABS as const, narrowed `stringnull args, a11y <label>→<span>). The test-side union is narrowed by typed helpers in game/tests/craft.test.ts (made/refused/isMade, which throw the refusal's own reason) — not a loose JSDoc on engine/craft.js, which was weighed and rejected as a fake green — plus piece(): Item & { q: number } since rollDrop always stamps q. noEmit: true in game/tsconfig.json clears the 8 allowJs "would overwrite input file" warnings over the shared engine/*.js`. Result: 0 errors, 0 warnings.game/src/App.svelte · game/src/sim/types.ts (ModLine.stat) · game/tests/*.test.ts · game/tsconfig.json · harness/todo.md C1
D-116applied · veto-ableThe two sizing follow-ups from the D-112 / D-114 re-base are closed. B23 — Grace is re-priced onto the same fraction its siblings keep. D-112 merged Dodge into Evasion after Grace had been sized against the old, narrower avoidance range, so the aura sat below the 80%-of-the-item-ceiling rule Iron Guard (Armour flat 32 of a 40 ceiling) and Energy Guard (Energy Shield flat 48 of a 60 ceiling) both hold. The Evasion item ceiling is evasion_flat's own 30, so Grace moves 12 → 24 — one line in tools/data/skills.json, re-printed by the skills writer, nothing else reads it. B24 — the Perfect dodge % band stays 1-3 and its derivation is re-stated so it reproduces from Cap 21. D-111 derived the band as 10% of caps.perfect_dodge (then 25); D-114 re-based that Cap to 21, and 10% of 21 is 2.1. The band cannot move to 1-2: a mod's bands array is the three quality bands with an equal Tier-slice count, and one slice per band spans at least three points (MP1), so a 3-band line whose range is 1-3 is structurally one point per band. The derivation is therefore restated as top = ceil(10% of caps.perfect_dodge) (ceil(2.1) = 3, and ceil(2.5) = 3 before), which reproduces the shipped band from the new Cap with no data change; the line's % is dead on a maxed-Lck build anyway because the Cap binds first (D-111). No mob_HP, curve or published combat number moves for either.tools/data/skills.json (aura.grace) · skill-pool-aura-heal.md (generated aura roster + §Sizing) · harness/todo.md B23 · B24
D-115applied · veto-ableThe starting character gets a flat base under each pool, and it closes A12. The owner named a starting character — 300 HP · 100 MP · 1,000 weight — and ruled that those three are base constants with the Core-stat bonus added on top, the same shape as HP and Mana: Max HP = hp_base + Vit × K_VIT_HP + level term, Max Mana = mana_base + Int × K_INT_MP + level term, capacity = weight_base + Str × K_STR_WEIGHT. Three keys land in level_gain: hp_base 300 · mana_base 100 · weight_base 1000, and the engine reads them everywhere a pool is built (DERIVED.hp/mana/weight, maxHpOf, maxManaOf, weightCapacityOf, es_cast_hp), so the client and the cages move together. What the bases move: level-1 HP 240 → 540, level-100 Vit-build HP 16,426 → 16,774, mana pool 3,624 → 3,724 (pool ÷ regen 39.5 → 40.6 sec, still inside the 40-sec intent tolerance), and weight capacity at level 1 is 1,024. That last number is what closes A12: the opening 35-weight sword now sits far under capacity, so the carried opening is untaxed — OP6 prints 0% and concept.md's Minute One block reads 1.3 sec both priced and carried (survive 378 sec), instead of the old 46% cut. A consequence worth the owner's eye: the encumbrance tax in formula-utility.md §11 is now non-binding — the heaviest printed set is 710 against a 1,016+ capacity at every level, so all three sets read 0%. The rule, the engine's encumbranceOf and the generated table all stand, and a heavier Base weight re-binds it without a doc edit, but the mechanic is dormant at these numbers; raising the weapon/armour weights or lowering weight_base is a balance move not taken here. doc_prose_lines_max held at 1,349 (the §11 bullet was re-worded to carry no number rather than raise the cap).tools/data/engine.json (level_gain) · tools/lib/registry.js · engine/index.js · tools/bases.js (capacities through the engine) · tools/check.js (opening block · OP3 · OP6) · formula-utility.md §11 · formula-defense.md §5 · concept.md (generated) · game/tests/bases-weight.test.ts · game/tests/weaponWeight.test.ts · harness/todo.md A12
D-114applied · owner rulingCore Stat % is retired — the ceiling is flat-only 510, and every K and Cap is re-based onto it. The owner removed the Core Stat % term (the Stat Mod % line): one item may roll at most 1 slot of Core stat = 25 Flat, all 12 items may roll the same stat, so the level-100 ceiling is stat_c 210 + 25×12 = 510, not the retired (210 + 300) × 1.60 = 816. Removing the multiply term is the largest single balance change in the project, so the caps and the curve were re-based onto the new number rather than left reachable only on paper: Evasion 80 · Perfect dodge 21 (the Lck ratio tops at 21.2% and the Cap now binds first, reachable at Lck 506) · Elemental res 45 · Alignment 35 · CDR 55 · aspd 500 (unchanged), and Accuracy keeps no Cap. K_INT_MREGEN moved 0.15 → 0.18 so the pool ÷ regen intent (40 sec) still holds at the smaller Int pool (3,624 ÷ 91.8 = 39.5 sec). mob_HP was re-read at the on-level DPS (8,881 at L100), so the 1-sec TTK anchor holds (11,901 ÷ (8,881 × 1.34) = 1.00 sec) and the no-skill entrant pays the multiplier as seconds. What the removal moved, and how each published promise was closed, is recorded as the closed rows of formula.md §0a. No player-facing Dodge text was touched — Perfect dodge and the mob-dodge line are outside this ruling.tools/data/engine.json (ceiling 510 · caps · K_INT_MREGEN) · tools/check.js (B-block · doc_prose_lines_max) · tools/{skills,survival,bases,loot}.js · formula.md §0a · formula-defense.md · formula-offense.md · formula-utility.md · checks.md · mod-pool.md · crafting.md · equipment-slot.md · equipment-slot-pools.md · equipment-slot-armor.md · equipment-slot-weapon.md · character-sheet.md · elements.md · world.md · loot.md · economy.md · towns-stalls.md

D-113applied · owner rulingThe data owns every number and the doc is its projection — one direction, enforced.

The owner asked how to make the game and the docs a single source of truth now that there is a playable page, and ruled for the proposal. The measurement that framed it: 5,981 numeric tokens sit inside the 68 generated blocks, and 4,232 sit in prose across 42 docs that no writer owns. A prose number cannot move when the data moves and nothing detects it going stale — which is exactly how Dodge flat 3-15 survived into files after the line was retired, and how the published ceiling stayed at 816 after Core Stat % was removed. Two changes, in the order that makes the second enforceable. First, the direction: X15 used to parse the "Total" column back out of mod-pool.md and compare it against the engine, which made the doc a second source of a number the engine already had — the two could disagree and the doc would win. It now reads mods.json, the file that owns the ranges, and only reports. The read-back rule for the retired K_dodge went with the key. Second, the ban: a number may only appear inside a BEGIN GENERATED marker; prose names the key (Int x K_INT_ES) and never the value. Gate L9 counts the lines that break it and fails when the count rises above engine.json doc_prose_lines_max. The cap lands at the measured 1,390, not at zero, because 1,390 prose lines break the rule today and a gate that fails on day one blocks every other pass without telling anyone anything new. It is a debt to lower, never a target to hit: every pass that fixes lines lowers the cap in the same edit, because a rule whose own text moves the count is not a rule. That mechanic proved itself within the hour — AGENT.md was edited to state the rule, which raised the count by 2 and L9 failed, and restoring skill-pool.md from git after a writer emptied it raised it by 20 more. Both were caught by the gate rather than by reading. Exempt: harness/decisions.md · harness/todo.md · harness/HARNESS.md (history and agent ops, which quote numbers as they were) and any line marked lint:allow. Still open and not fixed by this: combat.md lost ~140 lines of uncommitted prose when tools/survival.js --write overwrote the whole file, and skill-pool.md the same way; both were restored from git, which returns the committed version and not the owner’s working copy. A writer that can empty a doc is a second defect independent of this ruling — it should refuse to write when the marker pair is missing rather than truncate the file. | tools/check.js (X15 rewritten · L9 added) · tools/lib/engine.js (the K_dodge read-back removed) · tools/data/engine.json (doc_prose_lines_max · doc_prose) · AGENT.md · section 3 |

The owner named a 22-line roll list; measuring it against mods.json showed 16 already existed and 6 did not, so those 6 are what landed: Armour % 3-16 · Evasion % 3-16 · Life Regeneration flat 2-31 · Mana Regeneration flat 2-31 · Perfect dodge % 1-3 · Status Alignment resistance % 5-25. Every band is divided out of a number the design already publishes, not chosen: the two % defensive lines take Max HP % / Max Mana %'s own 3-16; the two regen flats top at +31, which is exactly what Life Regen % 15 and Mana Regen % 25 are worth at the ceiling (816 Vit × 0.25 = 204/sec, 816 Int × 0.15 = 122/sec), so each flat form equals its % form at the ceiling and carries the early game where the % has nothing to multiply; Perfect dodge % is 1-3 by elemental_alignment's own method — that line prices its % at 10% of its Cap (1-5 on Cap 50), and 10% of perfect dodge's Cap 25 is 2.5. Four engine signatures had to open, none invented: perfectDodgeChance takes a % (it scales the Lck line, so the Cap 25 still binds first and the % is dead on a maxed Lck build — 0.63% → 0.65% at Lck 12, 9.95% → 10.22% at Lck 210, and still 25.00% at Lck 816), hpRegenOf and manaRegenOf take a flat, and Armour/Evasion % multiply the finished rating inside player.ts. Status Alignment resistance is the ruling that overrules a standing ban: AGENT.md §5 said "do NOT bring back status res" and core-stats.md listed it under Removed, because it had been merged into Vit Elemental resistance (D-015). It is a Mod line and nothing else — a % cut on the 20% status proc in combat.md §5, read at rollStatus, worth 20% → 15% at the ceiling, which stretches the gap between status applications from 2.3 sec to 3.3 sec and drops burn from 88.8% uptime to 76%. It is not a Core stat, not a second resistance rating, and Elemental resistance still only ever covers the Element half of a hit; Holy veil stays the hard answer (timed immunity plus a cleanse) and this is the always-on one. Both files were amended rather than left contradicting the code. Not folded into mob_HP (H1) — six new lines on gear the player wears is unpriced player power, and checks.md D34 already carries that debt for the buffs; it is named there rather than silently added. Slot pools follow the Bases that already carry the flat form (Armour % on the five heavy Bases, Evasion % on the five light, Perfect dodge % beside Dodge), and the two regen flats plus the status line are Secondary on every Base. X15 now reads 25 maxima instead of 19, and MP3's skew list grew by the two regen flats at x1.50 — the same shape Accuracy and Attack speed % already sit at — while Status Alignment resistance was re-sliced to 7/7/6 so it does not become the worst offender in the table.tools/data/mods.json (6 rows) · tools/data/engine.json (mod_max 6 · mod_weights 6 rows) · tools/data/bases.json (slot pools) · engine/index.js (perfectDodgeChance · hpRegenOf · manaRegenOf) · game/src/sim/player.ts · game/src/sim/combat.ts (rollStatus) · game/src/sim/game.ts (the call site) · AGENT.md §5 · core-stats.md Removed · tools/check.js X15
D-109appliedA pool now spends only what stands in it, so nothing reads below nothing. The report was that the Mana and Energy Shield bars could go negative — and a negative pool is not a rounding to hide, it is state that has spent the same resource twice. The cause was the incoming split: mobSwing measured the shield against c.es, the sheet’s maximum, while the caller subtracted from the pool actually left, so a swing landing on a half-recharged shield took more than was there and drove the stored number under zero — and HP quietly absorbed less than it should have, because the hit had already been “paid for” twice. mobSwing now receives the live pool (an optional parameter defaulting to the sheet value, so every existing caller reads the same way) and clamps the split to it, which moves damage between the two pools instead of deleting any of it. tick also bounds both pools at the top of every second — never below nothing, never above what the sheet says they hold — because that is the state the bars print straight. Proof is two-sided: game/tests/poolFloors.test.ts shows one swing cannot spend more shield than stands and that the swing totals the same either way, then runs 3,000 seconds of hunting and reports the lowest shield and lowest mana it saw (0 and 48) with no negative and no over-full reading, and refuses to pass if the run never actually spent a pool. The running page was then stepped for 1,400 seconds and printed no minus anywhere — its lowest Energy Shield reading was exactly 0, which is the case that used to go under. One honesty note: the first version of that test also accused the game of reading the shield above its own maximum, and that was the test rebuilding the sheet without the buffs the tick feeds it, not a second defect.game/src/sim/combat.ts (mobSwing(…, liveEs)) · game/src/sim/game.ts (the call site · the per-second bound) · game/tests/poolFloors.test.ts (2 new tests)
D-108applied · veto-ableMinute one cannot lift what minute one is handed, and the cage now prints both figures instead of one. Building the main screen’s detail cards made the client weigh the starting weapon for the first time: openingGear built the opening sword with no weight field, so §11’s tax had nothing to bite and the opening character swung at full speed for free. With the piece weighed the way drops are weighed, the numbers say what they say: the opening one-handed sword is 35 against a level-1 capacity of 24 (Str × K_STR_WEIGHT), and the lightest main hand in the imported table is 25 — so no level-1 character carries any weapon untaxed, the cut is about 46% of aspd, and it sits inside the 50% Cap rather than against it. The curve’s published 1.3-second first kill is the untaxed figure; carried, the same character takes 2.5 seconds. Two things were done about that and one deliberately left alone. The weapon-weight rule moved into engine/index.js as weaponWeightOf(bases, name, slot) — the table is passed in because engine/ holds rules, not a second copy of the data — and the client’s call site is now a one-liner over it, so the cages and the game cannot diverge about minute one a second time. Gate OP6 measures the carried opening, fails if a weapon ever reads weightless or the tax escapes the Cap, and concept.md’s Minute One block prints both timings, so the doc no longer quotes a speed the client cannot produce. What was not done is turning a dial: raising K_STR_WEIGHT or the Base stat, lowering the floor of the weapon column D-101 imported from mod-pool.md, or re-pricing zone 1’s mob HP against the slower swing each move a published number, and OP2’s 0.8-2 second band still prices the untaxed character. D-107applied · veto-ableThe client now opens on one main screen: the combat scene, the character sheet, the carried inventory and the temporary inventory, all visible at once. The owner asked for the four regions on one screen with Melvor-style slot grids that can be sorted and switched between grid and list, and PoE-style hover detail with the equip decision in the card. The screen is a three-column layout — the fight wide across the top, the two bags under it, the sheet as a sidebar that keeps its place — collapsing to one column on a narrow window, and the two tabs that used to hold that content (character, bag) are gone rather than duplicated. Three new pieces of plumbing, all in the sim where the tests can reach them: ui/bag.ts builds the slot view model and its five orders (as it dropped · by slot · by Rarity · by strength · by name), taking Rarity order and quality order out of loot.RARITY and loot.BANDS and strength out of loot.score, so the panel owns no ranking of its own; sim/slots.ts gained bagStacks, which slotsUsed now counts, so the drawn grid and the used / available number cannot disagree; and sim/craft.ts keeps the line names coming from mods.json, so the card prints the Mod names the docs use. The detail card is where the decisions live: every line with its Tier and Element, what the piece weighs, how it compares with the piece worn in that slot, the Stat Mod's stat choice, and the Equip button — and nothing equips itself (D-089), so equipping stays a press and the card closes on the press because the piece it described has left the bag. The bag filter's own thresholds moved under the temporary inventory as a fold-out, since that is the pile they decide the fate of. The scene's bar row now shows the four values character-sheet.md prescribes — Energy Shield above HP while it is present, HP, Mana, Attack speed as hits per second, and Weight with the aspd it costs — which it did not before. Proof is by driving the running page rather than by a picture: the in-app browser surface reports no positive viewport, so a screenshot cannot be taken there, and what was measured instead is geometry and behaviour — the three named columns at their grid areas, 46×46 square slots, exactly 12 · 50 · 30 slot positions drawn, the sort orders provably differing, list mode rendering rows, the hover card opening inside the viewport with the Rarer border colour, a Stat Mod pick sticking, and an Equip moving a piece from the temporary bag into the worn grid (worn going 1 → 2 and that same piece reading as worn in the sidebar) with no console errors. Client build and the suite are green (12 cages · 258 tests); character-sheet.md and loot.md §4 gained the display rules so the screen and the docs say the same thing.game/src/ui/SlotGrid.svelte · game/src/ui/ItemDetail.svelte · game/src/ui/bag.ts · game/src/sim/slots.ts (bagStacks) · game/src/App.svelte (main screen · retired tabs · bar row) · character-sheet.md · loot.md §4
D-106applied · veto-ableP0-2’s deferred rebalance was measured on geared characters, and the hit-count build stayed itself. The line promised that Agi’s value comes from hit count — proc per hit, DoT tick, chill, with Riposte as its boss path — and sent the numbers to the mob-sheet pass, which D-103 has now run. game/tests/gearedB1.test.ts measures both builds off one hunt: the same seed, the same drops, the same zone, and then the bag spent two ways on two clones of that instant — one rebuilt slot by slot around the lines that feed swings (aspd · accuracy · Alignment · dodge), one around the lines that feed a single heavy press (Str · physical power · crit), each Stat Mod told the stat its theme buys through the same chosenStat field the panel writes. Damage is credited where it is dealt — counters.damageBy splits the swing, the press and the status ticking over time — so the reading says what the damage is made of, not just how much of it there is. The result: the hit-count build reaches ×0.87 of the big-hit build and 69% of its damage arrives through a swing or something a swing left behind, against 58% the other way, so the two builds are genuinely different shapes rather than two routes to one number, and no curve value moved (the policy stays: nothing is nerfed to close a gap the design already priced). Two honest caveats ride with it. The big-hit reading is the weaker comparison because the bag simply held more swing-themed pieces — seven decisions rebuilt that side against two on this one — so ×0.87 is this bag’s ratio, not a published constant. And the leg that came out thin is the one the promise leans on hardest: the statuses those swings plant are barely a percent or two of the build’s damage at the level cap, which is a decision to make rather than a number to type, so it is queued as B22 with the two ways out and the reason it cannot be settled quietly (the DoT budget was already folded into mob_HP by D-094).game/tests/gearedB1.test.ts (second reading · huntTo · Theme) · game/src/sim/game.ts (credit · counters.damageBy) · game/src/sim/types.ts · concept.md P0-2 · harness/todo.md B22
D-105applied · veto-ableA mob skill’s burst shape is bounded by the pool, so the survival cage can gate the re-timing without a skill list existing. D-067 ruled mob skills a re-timing of the mob’s own priced mob_PS and combat.md §5b said the cage would keep modelling the steady average “until a future cage models the burst shape” — but the species skill lists that would name a window do not exist yet, and inventing one to test against would have put a made-up number in front of a published rule. The bound needs no invention: a burst that spends S seconds of budget in one instant empties a target only once S exceeds the pool measured in that mob’s own seconds of damage, so SV8 computes pool-seconds for every AFK-reachable shape (normal · group of 5 · elite against all four reference builds, after dodge, resistance and armour) and fails if any of them can absorb less than two seconds of its own damage. The measured margin is far from the line — the thinnest is the dodge build against an elite, and the number is printed by the gate rather than typed into prose — which is the useful reading: a designer can give a mob a two-second wind-up, a five-second chanter or a sixteen-second telegraph and none of them can become a one-hit kill, and the moment a shape wants more than the pool holds, the cage says so. The steady-average tables are untouched (checks.md D6-D14 read the same blocks), and the promise lands as checks.md D35 with SV8 as its judge, per H’s own rule that every multiplier is written as a row in group D and let the cages decide.tools/survival.js (SV8 · table(kind, label, gearMod)) · combat.md §5b · checks.md D35

DoT stays outside both steps because status.mob_side says burn/poison/bleed land in full and formula-offense.md §4 says armour does not reduce bleed. B14: town.json prices Herb pouch II at 60 m and III at 240 m as kind: "space" lines and farm.md said the pouch "raises the herb stack ceiling" while also printing a 999 stack that engine.json inventory.stack_size says is 100 — the same fact in two places with two values, and no ladder number anywhere. Rather than invent a ceiling, the pouch does what its own kind says: each tier adds one slot to the character bag (character_slot_grant: 1, the same unit a stash tab is sold in), so slotsAvailable = inventory.character_slots + bought space. B16: save.md promised to store "allocated stat points" although no rule produces them (formula.md §1 derives every Core stat from level and gear; D-042 defers per-skill stat assignment past release), so that phrase is gone from the Character row and the reason is written beside it — building an allocation system would be a new power source, which AGENT.md §5 forbids doing quietly. B6 · B7: the owner's permit that a weapon type may carry several Bases stands, but no variant list has been written, so the new bases gate BS9 asserts the shipped frames are exactly the 12 types and fails if a frame list ever appears without reaching bases.json and the drop roll together. towns-stalls.md was re-printed from the data, so the stall table now carries the new note instead of a hand-typed one.tools/data/town.json · tools/bases.js (BS9) · game/src/sim/slots.ts · game/src/App.svelte · farm.md · save.md · towns-stalls.md (generated)
D-091applied · veto-ableThe character bag is a real bag, and a seed is a herb. Two queue items closed with numbers the design already carries, so nothing new was priced. B15: engine.json already publishes character_slots 30, stack_size (stones 999 · herbs 100 · potions 100), gold_uses_slot false and the overflow verb stop_pickup, yet the client counted every medium as an unbounded number. game/src/sim/slots.ts now charges one slot per full or partial stack and refuses a grant that would need a slot the bag does not have — and a producer checks first, so brewing or condensing never eats herbs and stones for a bottle that cannot be carried. The verb is the doc's own: nothing is deleted, nothing is converted into another medium, and the refusals are counted (counters.stopped) and shown. B11: farm.md opens the cycle with "plant 1 seed → 4 h → harvest 3", and no seed exists anywhere else, so the seed is one herb of the tier being planted (farm.seed_cost_herbs, the doc's own "1") — the cycle becomes 3-for-1 instead of 3-for-0, which makes the two taps a day a choice about stock rather than free growth, and keeps herb output the only thing the farm produces. Measured consequence: the AFK pacing run is unchanged (the mint still pays every hour and the kill rate is still 1.00× the band's published figure), because thirty slots of 999-stone stacks is never the binding constraint on stones; it binds on herbs and draughts, which is what the pouch ladder (B14) is supposed to raise.game/src/sim/slots.ts · game/src/sim/{farm,game,types}.ts · engine/farm.js · tools/data/engine.json (farm.seed_cost_herbs) · game/tests/slots.test.ts · game/tests/farm.test.ts · farm.md (unchanged)
D-090owner ruling · appliedElemental damage is per Element, like PoE. Answering "one Element per item or per line" with like PoE, each Elemental line keeps its own Element and the counter table is now applied per pool, not to one chosen Element of the piece: a weapon holding fire and cold added damage hits a fire monster with ×1.5 weak on the fire part and the fire↔cold pair on the cold part, in the same swing. sumLines keeps the aggregate lines it already had (elemFlat · elemPct) so the total Elemental pool is byte-for-byte the old number, and adds a breakdown by Element; buildCharacter exposes elemByElement, attributing the K_ELEM base to the piece's own Element and parking anything no line names in an unattributed pool that is never countered either way. playerSwing sums the countered pools instead of multiplying one. The old weaponElement stays as the display line ("carrying fire") because the 12 types still have no Element column and crafting.md forbids locking one. Measured: the AFK run's kill rate is unchanged at 1.00× the band's published figure, so the split moved distribution, not power — which is what B19 needed to stay out of the balance audit's way. Closes harness/todo.md B19.game/src/sim/{player,combat}.ts · game/tests/element.test.ts
D-089owner ruling · appliedNothing equips itself, and the player chooses whether to travel. Asked the three open questions, the owner answered "no auto pick", "like PoE" on Element, and "have toggle stay or forward". So D-087's auto-wear is reverted: an upgrade keep stays in the bag as the decision it is, and the character only wears what it was told to wear. Two consequences were then fixed without inventing a number. First, the filter's bar is now the best piece the character holds for that slot, worn or waiting, so a drop that merely matches a decision already in the bag dissolves for its one stone instead of filling the bag with near-duplicates. Second, a full bag no longer throws away a genuinely better piece: the weakest kept piece of that slot is swapped out and dissolves, and only a slot the bag does not represent at all is a real spill (loot.md §4's pause is now "you must go and equip", not "your bag is full of old news"). Measured in game/tests/pacing.test.ts: the Reroll mint pays +28 → +56 an hour across six hours (it was zero after minute 34 under auto-pause), and the run still leaves 50-95 pieces an hour on the floor — the honest cost of a player who does not clear the bag, kept as a gate so the number cannot quietly disappear. travel is stored per character, default stay; on forward the character walks to the next already-opened settlement once its level passes the current zone's own levels top (mob.zones, no new number), which is zone selection rather than Road travel, so the Road staying opt-in and online-only is untouched.game/src/sim/game.ts · game/src/sim/types.ts · game/src/state/save.ts · game/src/App.svelte · game/tests/{travel,pacing}.test.ts
D-088applied · veto-ableThe Element counter now fires, on the Element half only. Two defects hid it: the sim called playerSwing(..., weaponElement = null) forever, so elements.md's counter table and the ×1.5 weak line never ran anywhere in the client; and when a multiplier was passed, damage *= weakOrCounter applied it to the whole hit, including the physical half — which combat.md §2 and D-030 assign to Armour, not to Elements ("Knight and Golem are answered by Armour and chill, Seraph and Slime only by Elemental resistance"). The held weapon's Element is read from the piece's own stored Elemental line (the 12 types carry no Element column, and crafting.md forbids locking one), steps 3-4 scale only elem × alignment/100, and Chaos is exempt from the weak line because the doc states it is "the only Element with no counter" and gets 1.15 even against itself — which the code derives from the table (the Element whose row is constant) instead of naming it. Measured consequence, with no design number touched: the AFK loop moved from 0.89× to 0.97× the band's published kill rate, so the published figure already assumed elemental play and B1's "full-Element damage ~10-15%" uplift is now a measured number instead of an estimate. harness/todo.md B19 records the one thing this pass had to choose rather than read: the docs say item Element, the drop roll assigns Element per line.game/src/sim/{player,combat,game}.ts · game/src/App.svelte · game/tests/element.test.ts
D-087applied · veto-ableA kept upgrade is worn at once, the way the loot model has always counted it. tools/loot.js replaces equipped[slot] on every keep, and that is the whole reason its keep-rate falls from ~28/hr in hour one to under 1/hr by hour 6 (loot.md §3). The client did not: it stored keeps in the adventure bag and left the character in opening gear forever, so 88% of drops read as "keep" (the bar never rose), the 50-slot bag filled at minute 34, and because §4 pauses pickups when the bag is full the Reroll value mint — the medium every craft is priced in — went to 0 per hour for the rest of the run (the B17 dead end). Now the upgrade verdict equips directly (an empty slot of that kind first, else the worn piece the filter compared against), and the displaced piece dissolves for the same 1 Reroll value stone a reject earns, because a piece that just lost to a better one is definitionally not an upgrade; it also counts toward the 500-piece tier-stone milestone. A piece kept only for an Element the player cannot resist yet is still stored, not worn, and the Collector's hold still runs first. No number was invented or changed — the stone-per-piece rule, the margin, the milestone and the funnel are the ones already published. Measured after the change (game/tests/pacing.test.ts): the mint pays in every hour (+40 → +103), kills climb to 1,049/hr (0.89× the band's published figure over six hours, the residual being the Lck and zone progression that audit B1 owns), and the bag only fills at 119 min while income keeps running.game/src/sim/game.ts (wear · dissolve) · game/tests/pacing.test.ts · game/tests/mastery.test.ts (its invariant restated for a weapon that changes mid-run)
D-086applied · veto-ableA curse now writes its numbers on the mob it lands on. Five curse rows (weaken · blinding_mark · expose · cripple · jinx) state a plain target-side modifier, so they carry effects with subject: "target" and the same verbatim-value rule the self-buffs got (cage S11 widened to check the subject and the new stat names, S12 now prints 36 prose-only rows). game/src/sim/curse.ts holds the store — mob spawn id → line → value and seconds — and the roster's own refresh precedent decides stacking: a re-cast of the same line refreshes it, two different lines on one mob add. Both combat directions read it: a mob's threat is priced as ps, so damage dealt −25% and aspd −20% compound onto one multiplier (×0.60 together), accuracy −30% feeds the hit roll and the dodge roll it opposes, damage taken +20% and crit chance +15% land on our swing against that mob alone, and the mob's HP is not touched so nothing moves mob_HP (H1). sunder was left in prose on purpose: a mob's Elemental resistance is exactly the open question harness/todo.md B8 asks the owner, and modelling one curse by answering it silently would be the wrong way to settle it. The combat panel gained an "Under a curse" column and the PS column now shows the cursed number, so what the player reads is what the fight uses. No published number moved.tools/data/skills.json · tools/lib/roster.js · engine/skills.js · game/src/sim/{curse,combat,skills,game,types}.ts · game/src/App.svelte · skill-pool-curse.md (unchanged)
D-085applied · veto-ableA skill's stated magnitude becomes a number the game can spend. The roster's effect sentence was the only home for every non-attack skill's strength (harness/todo.md B9), so the client cast buffs that changed nothing, auras that reserved mana for nothing, and read a heal's percentage out of prose — which had quietly turned Greater Heal into a 45%-per-second drip over eight seconds instead of one instant 45%. tools/data/skills.json now carries effects: [{stat, op, value}] on the rows whose sentence states a plain self-modifier (10 rows: 6 auras · 2 buffs · 2 heals), with every value copied verbatim out of its own effect text, and the skill cage enforces that: S11 fails if any declared number stops appearing in its row's sentence or uses a stat outside the closed set, and S12 prints how many rows are still prose-only so the remainder cannot be forgotten. engine/skills.js aggregateEffects is the single fold (percent and flat lines add, mult lines compound) and buildCharacter spends it, so aura.iron_guard moves Armour by exactly its row's number and Warcry's ×1.20 on Elemental resistance lands inside the existing Cap rather than past it — resistanceOf and alignmentOf gained a trailing multiplier for exactly that. Two rules followed from reading, not inventing: the aura block is exclusive (reserving the whole pool would leave nothing to cast with, so toggleTrack refuses at the limit, and the duplicated reserve sum in the UI is gone), and rows whose numbers have no home yet (Berserker's leech, the Heralds' per-Element damage, every curse's target-side arithmetic) were left in prose rather than half-modelled. No published number moved.tools/data/skills.json · tools/lib/roster.js (S11 · S12) · engine/skills.js · engine/index.js · game/src/sim/{player,skills,combat,game}.ts · game/src/App.svelte
D-084applied · veto-ableThe win condition is in the game, and it is derived rather than quoted. concept.md settles completion on killing the final zone's boss inside a single spawn without being Pushed, and nothing in the client tracked it: a boss died for stones and that was the end of it. engine/index.js gains finalZoneId · winTarget, which read the last row of mob.zones, that zone's level ceiling, its named boss from mob.bosses, and HP from the same mobHpAt curve the spawn uses — so the figure the panel prints (Vermolch Ninefold Choir · level 90 · HP 160,635) is the figure the fight rolls and equals the number concept.md publishes without copying it. game/src/sim/goal.ts owns the two conditions: the gate arms on that boss's spawn before the first swing of the tick, and closes only if the Push counter has not moved since (combat.md §7: losing costs the spawn, so a walk-back is a failed attempt rather than a partial one). A boss that leaves alive voids the arming. Only the first completion is recorded and the run keeps going, because concept.md rules out prestige. The record is additive state, so the save version stays where it is and migrate backfills it — unlike D-083, where the new fields changed what existing systems store.engine/index.js · tools/lib/engine.js · game/src/sim/{goal,game,types}.ts · game/src/state/save.ts · game/src/App.svelte · concept.md (unchanged)
D-083applied · veto-ableThe bag filter is configurable per slot, and a snapshot is owed before a bad file can cost a character. loot.md §4 says the filter is configurable and save.md says the thresholds are stored per slot; neither could be true while the client hard-coded one margin and passed an empty Element set, which also meant the Element keep-reason could never fire — no dropped line carried an Element at all. Three changes followed: every Elemental line now stores its Element (rolled from elements.order, same as the loot cage already did, and never derived from a resistance number because crafting must not change it), game/src/sim/filter.ts holds one rule per slot (margin · Rarity floor · the Element switch) defaulting to loot.filter.upgrade_margin_pct so a raised threshold is a player setting and not a second copy of the number, and the "Elements/slots not yet found" list is stored from the gear actually worn. save.md item 5 then became real: engine.json save carries the snapshot count, the interval and the trigger list, writeSave takes a snapshot outside the record it protects, and a restore rewinds the character whole and rebuilds the shared account record from the surviving slots — which is the shape save.md item 3 requires (a rewind, not a discard of the last craft). tools/loot.js now calls the shared keepsDrop instead of carrying its own copy of the same comparison, and the save format is SCHEMA_VERSION = 3 because both new fields are stored state. No published number moves: LT11/LT12 print the identical keep-rates before and after the shared call.tools/data/engine.json (save · loot.filter.rules) · engine/loot.js · engine/craft.js · tools/loot.js · game/src/sim/{filter,snapshot,drop,craft,game}.ts · game/src/state/save.ts · save.md · loot.md (both unchanged)
D-082applied · veto-ableOffline, salvage and the boss clock are now enforced by data, not by luck. Three numbers save.md depends on existed only as prose and are copied verbatim into engine.json: rarity.floor_ceiling (item-rarity.md's floor/ceiling table — so an offline drop can never come in below its zone's floor, which is the anti-cheat save.md item 6 asks for), salvage.pieces_per_tier_stone = 500 (loot.md §5 · checks.md F15), and the boss interval read back out of loot.boss_per_hour rather than typed. Two behaviours followed: the boss is now a stored due time per character that does not advance while offline (a modulo on the tick let a busy second skip a spawn and hand the next one out early), and craft.reroll floors at the highest value the slot ever held (item.baselines), not the value it holds now, so a 1-stone randomize that lands lower cannot be re-rolled upward for free. The save format carries SCHEMA_VERSION = 2 and an import at any other version is rejected, not converted (save.md item 4), and a shared account record keeps the best Mastery across the three slots while currencies stay per character. No published number moves: F7-F9 read the same boss rate, and F15 was already the rule.tools/data/engine.json (rarity · salvage) · engine/craft.js · game/src/state/save.ts · save.md (unchanged)

D-076applied · veto-ableTask sizing lives in town.json, not in code. tasks.md deliberately leaves N and the reward count to the rebalance pass ("N scales with zone group size", "reward ~15 min of §5 income"), but the client cannot run a board on prose, so the numbers were written down as data: task_sizing carries hunt_n_anchor 5 (read straight from engine.json opening.first_rule, which is a 5-kill hunt in zone 1's 1-2 group), the rule N = round(anchor × group upper ÷ 2), elite_n 3 (the middle of the published 2-4), reward_minutes_of_band_income 15, the boss payout (1 Remove or 4 Reroll tier, the winner's choice as tasks.md writes it), 3 slots and the 1-hour refill. The reward is then computed by engine/index.js taskPayout(band, minutes) from the band's own stone income, so a drop-rate change moves task payouts with it and the client holds no copy. Two side rulings the same pass forced: junk is now kept and sold by hand at the Counterhand (gold is never auto-credited on a kill, per economy.md), and the Elite stone lines (elite_tier_stones 0.05 · elite_add_stone_chance 0.00625) are read as expected values per kill, so the client rolls them as a chance to pay one whole stone — the published per-hour rates are unchanged and the ledger stays integer. Changing any of these moves no doc number: towns-stalls.md prints stall prices, not task sizes, and checks.md E5 is untouched.tools/data/town.json (task_sizing) · engine/index.js (stonesForMinutes · taskPayout) · harness/todo.md §B

Mastery is a per-weapon side track and not a build-calculation stat (DPS is never touched, D-065), so it stays off the twelve-item main read and lives on the weapon panel. Owner ruling on harness/todo.md A9 (towns-stalls.md section 8 · checks.md T15): do not add a per-settlement frame_weight to town.json. tools/loot.js had already measured what a weight would cost (armored x2.5 / cloth x0.4 pushes the high-band keep-rate 0.81% → 0.72%), and the owner chose not to pay it, so the Base-bias column becomes permanent flavour and there is no keep-rate re-sim to wait for.
